acceptance: tests/unit/core/throughput/test_stream_timing.py verifies that connection setup and teardown durations are excluded from stream.duration, start_time/end_time, and start_wall_time/end_wall_time deterministically without depending on real-time CPU speed (< 0.1s wall sleep margin).
A regression check confirms the test fails if setup or close time is moved inside the measured stream window.
The test passes 50+ consecutive iterations without flakes and make pr-preflight passes on the merged head.

description:
## Problem
`tests/unit/core/throughput/test_stream_timing.py::test_tpch_stream_window_excludes_connection_setup_and_close` and `test_tpcds_stream_window_excludes_connection_setup_and_close` (both using `_SlowSetupConnection` and `_assert_window_excludes_setup_and_teardown`) sleep `0.2s` in `__init__` and `close()` and assert that real elapsed execution time for 22 mock queries is `< 0.2 / 2` (`0.1s`). Under CPU contention on hosted CI runners, 22 mock queries took `0.110s` on PR #4487 (`job/138504495685`), causing an unrelated red `core` check.

## Change
Replace real `time.sleep` timing margins in both `test_tpch_stream_window_excludes_connection_setup_and_close` and `test_tpcds_stream_window_excludes_connection_setup_and_close` in `tests/unit/core/throughput/test_stream_timing.py` with a deterministic controllable clock (monkeypatching the monotonic clock and wall-clock time source read by the throughput runner so setup advances the clock by e.g. `10.0s`, query execution advances by `0.001s`, and close advances by `10.0s`), preserving full coverage of both monotonic `duration` and `start_wall_time`/`end_wall_time` exclusion while eliminating real-time runner jitter and speeding up the fast suite.

## Decision gates
- Do not skip, xfail, quarantine, or simply weaken the assertion without proving setup and teardown remain strictly excluded from the timed window.
- Do not change production timing behavior (`benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time()` / `elapsed_seconds()`) unless a real production bug is found; if one is found, report it before broadening scope.

## Verification rubric
- Pass: running `uv run -- pytest tests/unit/core/throughput/test_stream_timing.py` 50 times in a loop passes 50/50 with sub-second total runtime; manually advancing the fake clock inside query execution or moving setup inside the window causes both TPC-H and TPC-DS tests to fail; `make pr-preflight` passes.
- Fail: either test still depends on `time.sleep` vs wall-clock CPU speed, or passes when setup/teardown is erroneously included in `stream.duration`.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Follow BenchBox timing invariants (`benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time()` / `elapsed_seconds()`). No explanatory comments or docstrings in first-party Python (`make comment-policy-check`). Stage named paths only; commit with pinned human Git identity and no agent attribution. Heavy work only via `make pr-preflight` / `make heavy-run`; never bypass `~/.benchbox/test.lock`. Open with `make pr-open`, arm with `make pr-arm`, and monitor to merge.
